key_insight: Distributed fault-tolerant quantum computing can substantially reduce physical qubits per node with just one communication channel per node, but at roughly tenfold longer execution time under the studied assumptions.
engineering_relevance: The analysis quantifies trade-offs among processor size, quantum-link performance, and runtime when scaling interconnected superconducting processors.
method: Analyze fault-tolerant computing resources for superconducting processors connected by microwave or optical links.
Assess computational performance under limited remote Bell-pair generation resources.
Evaluate trade-offs involving Bell-pair fidelity, generation rate, and communication multiplexing.
evidence_signal: The resource analysis finds substantial per-node qubit savings with one physical channel per node under forward-looking microwave-link assumptions of 1 MHz Bell-pair generation and 90% fidelity.
watch_item: These are resource-analysis results, not an experimental demonstration; reducing runtime overhead requires higher Bell-pair fidelity and extensive multiplexing.
paper_title: Feasibility of Distributed Fault-Tolerant Quantum Computing: From Quantum Links to Algorithms
